1	# graph — Requirement Capture
2	
3	**Stage:** Need · **Output:** `requirement@1`
4	
5	Converts raw need statements into structured, testable requirements. Asks one clarifying question at a time until a spec writer could produce an accurate spec from the requirement alone.
6	
7	---

9	## Subagents
10	
11	| Subagent | Role | Tier | Description |
12	| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
13	| `graph-intake` | Intake Structurer | haiku/low | Converts free text into a `requirement@1` draft. Infers all fields it can; leaves gaps noted in `reasoning`. |

15	| `graph-auditor` | Auditor | sonnet/medium | Cross-references a completed `requirement@1` against stated stakeholder needs to confirm it is complete and internally consistent. |

18

20	[free text] → graph-intake → graph-clarifier (× N) → graph-auditor → requirement@1
21	```

1	# canon — Specification
2	
3	**Stage:** Spec · **Output:** `spec@1`
4	
5	Drafts, audits, and gates unambiguous, testable specifications. A spec that exits canon can be handed to a developer who has never spoken to the product team and implemented without clarifying questions.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Subagents
10	
11	| Subagent | Role | Tier | Description |
12	| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
13	| `canon-drafter` | Drafter | sonnet/medium | Produces a `spec@1` from a `requirement@1` and optional `research-report@1`. No TBDs permitted. |
14	| `canon-auditor` | Auditor | sonnet/medium | Adversarially reviews the spec for vague criteria, missing error cases, and unverifiable claims. |
15	| `canon-verifier` | Drift Detector | sonnet/medium | Checks whether an existing spec still matches the current code — detects spec drift. |
16	| `canon-exit-gate` | Exit Gate | opus/high | Final pass/fail verdict before the spec enters planning. Default disposition: fail. |
17	
18	## Pipeline
19	
20	```
21	requirement@1 [+ research-report@1] → canon-drafter → canon-auditor → canon-exit-gate → spec@1
22	```
23	
24	`canon-verifier` runs independently against an existing spec and codebase to detect drift.
25	
26	## Gates
27	
28	The exit gate enforces four conditions:
29	1. Every acceptance criterion is a testable proposition
30	2. No TBDs remain
31	3. Error cases have `is_error_case: true`
32	4. Scope fits a single planning cycle
33	
34	On fail, blockers are returned to `canon-drafter` for targeted retry (max 3).
35	
36	## Output Schema
37	
38	`spec@1` — see `shared/schemas/spec@1.json`
39

41

2	
3	**Stage:** Plan · **Output:** `plan@1`
4	
5	Decomposes a `spec@1` into a sequenced, testable implementation plan. Every task is self-contained — an implementer with no domain knowledge can execute it without making a design decision.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Subagents
10	
11	| Subagent | Role | Tier | Description |
12	| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
13	| `vector-planner` | Planner | sonnet/medium | Decomposes the spec into ordered tasks, each with exact file paths, a failing test, minimal implementation, and a conventional commit message. |
14	| `vector-estimator` | Estimator | sonnet/medium | Produces per-task time estimates, identifies parallelizable tasks, and lists blocking dependencies. |
15	| `vector-challenger` | Challenger | opus/high | Adversarially reviews the plan for missing tasks, wrong ordering, under-specified steps, and missing error handling. |
16	
17	## Pipeline
18	
19	```
20	spec@1 → vector-planner → vector-challenger → [vector-estimator] → plan@1
21	```
22

24

26	
27	Every task in `plan@1` must include:
28	- Exact file paths to create or modify
29	- A failing test written before any implementation code
30	- The command to run the test with expected failure output
31	- The minimal implementation that makes the test pass
32	- A conventional commit message
33	
34	No TBDs. No "the implementer will decide."
35

1	# lambda — Implementation
2	
3	**Stage:** Code · **Output:** `changeset@1`
4	
5	Executes implementation tasks from a `plan@1` using TDD. Each task is implemented by a fresh subagent with isolated context. An adversarial exit gate verifies the complete implementation before producing a `changeset@1`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Subagents
10	
11	| Subagent | Role | Tier | Description |
12	| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
13	| `lambda-recon` | Workspace Recon | haiku/low | Discovers test runner, build tool, and baseline test state before any code is written. |
14	| `lambda-implementer` | Implementer | sonnet/medium | Executes one task: writes the failing test, implements the minimal code to pass, commits. |
15	| `lambda-reviewer` | Reviewer | sonnet/medium | Post-task code review — checks for missed sibling functions, severity of code quality issues, and regressions. |
16	| `lambda-exit-gate` | Exit Gate | opus/high | Adversarially verifies the complete implementation: all acceptance criteria implemented and tested, all tests pass, no regressions. |
17	
18	## Pipeline
19	
20	```
21	plan@1 → lambda-recon → [lambda-implementer → lambda-reviewer] × N tasks → lambda-exit-gate → changeset@1
22	```
23	
24	Each task runs in a fresh `lambda-implementer` context. The reviewer runs after each task. The exit gate runs once after all tasks.
25	
26	## TDD Cycle (per task)
27	
28	1. Write failing test → confirm it fails
29	2. Write minimal implementation → confirm test passes
30	3. Run full test suite → confirm no regressions
31	4. Commit
32	
33	## Output Schema
34	
35	`changeset@1` — see `shared/schemas/changeset@1.json`
36	
37	Required: `summary`, `files_changed`, `acceptance_criteria_met`
38	
39	## Next Stage
40

1	# axiom — Verification Gate
2	
3	**Stage:** Gate · **Output:** `verdict@1`
4	
5	A reusable, artifact-agnostic verification gate. Any artifact type (spec, plan, changeset, finding report) can be run through axiom. Produces a definitive `verdict@1` — pass or fail with specific, actionable blockers.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Subagents
10	
11	| Subagent | Role | Tier | Description |
12	| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
13	| `axiom-recon` | Artifact Recon | haiku/low | Builds the verification manifest: artifact path, criteria to check, source files to read. No judgment. |
14	| `axiom-verifier` | Verifier | sonnet/medium | Reads each source file and classifies every criterion as `verified`, `failed`, or `unverifiable`. Neutral — reports evidence, not verdicts. |
15	| `axiom-exit-gate` | Exit Gate | opus/high | Produces a final `verdict@1`. Default: fail. Unverifiable criteria are treated as failures unless explicitly waived. |
16	
17	## Pipeline
18	
19	```
20	artifact + criteria → axiom-recon → axiom-verifier → axiom-exit-gate → verdict@1
21	```
22	
23	## Retry Protocol
24	
25	On `fail`, the orchestrator returns the `blockers` array directly to the producing agent for a targeted patch (not a full regeneration). On retry 2, escalate to a higher-effort model. After 3 retries, escalate to the human.
26	
27	`retry_count` is tracked in `verdict@1` and incremented by the exit gate on each pass.
28	
29	## Output Schema
30	
31	`verdict@1` — see `shared/schemas/verdict@1.json`
32	
33	Fields: `verdict` (pass/fail), `confidence`, `blockers[]`, `verdict_summary` (≤300 chars), `artifact_type`, `retry_count`
34	
35	## Usage
36	
37	Axiom gates run automatically within `canon` (spec gate) and `lambda` (implementation gate). Run axiom standalone to gate any artifact outside the standard pipeline.
38	
[/external_agent_tool_result]

1	# proof — Adversarial Bug Hunting
2	
3	**Stage:** Cross-cutting · **Output:** `finding-report@1`
4	
5	Adversarial bug hunting on live code. Builds a reachability manifest to exclude dead code, scans live files for hazard patterns, adversarially refutes each candidate, and gates the output through an exit verifier.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Subagents
10	
11	| Subagent | Role | Tier | Description |
12	| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
13	| `proof-recon` | Module Manifest Builder | haiku/low | Traces imports from entry points to build a live/dead file manifest. Scanners only operate on live files. |
14	| `proof-scanner` | Hazard Scanner | sonnet/medium | Scans live files for bug patterns across 6 hazard taxonomies. Returns candidates with trigger conditions. |
15	| `proof-adversary` | Adversarial Verifier | opus/high | Tries to refute each candidate by reading actual code and tracing control flow. A finding confirms only when no refutation can be constructed. |
16	| `proof-exit-gate` | Exit Verifier | opus/high | Verifies the final finding report is complete and consistent before passing it downstream. |
17	
18	## Pipeline
19	
20	```
21	workspace → proof-recon → proof-scanner → proof-adversary → proof-exit-gate → finding-report@1
22	```
23	
24	## Dead Code Exclusion
25	
26	`proof-recon` traces imports from all entry points to build a live file set. Any file not reachable from any entry point is classified as dead and excluded from scanning. This prevents false positives from unused code paths.
27

30	`finding-report@1` — see `shared/schemas/finding-report@1.json`
